``` ### CSS Styling Specifications ```css /* Base styles */ body { font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; margin: 2.5cm; /* Standard print margins */ line-height: 1.5; color: #333; max-width: 100%; hyphens: auto; } /* Page setup for A4 */ @page { size: A4; margin: 2.5cm; } /* Chapter headings */ .chapter { page-break-before: always; margin-top: 3cm; } .chapter-number { font-size: 2em; font-weight: bold; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.1em; margin-bottom: 0.5em; } .chapter-title { font-size: 1.5em; font-weight: normal; margin-bottom: 1em; } /* Transitions */ .transition { font-style: italic; margin: 2em 0; padding: 1em 2em; border-left: 3px solid #ccc; background: #f9f9f9; } /* Page numbers */ @bottom-center { content: counter(page); font-size: 0.9em; color: #666; } /* Headers */ @top-left { content: "The Future is Unwritten"; font-size: 0.8em; color: #999; } @top-right { content: "Robert Mills"; font-size: 0.8em; color: #999; } ``` ### Special Elements - **Transitions**: 10-20 sentence passages between chapters - **Historical context**: Integrated seamlessly into narrative - **Physiological effects**: Described in accessible, engaging language - **Images**: Placeholder positions with captions - **Drop caps**: First letter of each chapter enlarged and styled - **Part openings**: Special formatting for major section divisions ## Phase 3: Image Generation ### Image Types Required 1. **Cover Image** - Professional, eye-catching design 2. **Chapter Illustrations** - One per chapter (black and white sketches) 3. **Epilogue Image** - Reflective closing image ### Prompt Engineering Approach For each image, create specific prompts based on chapter content: **Cover Prompt Structure:** ``` Create a professional book cover for the memoir "[TITLE]" by [AUTHOR]. The cover should feature: - [Key visual elements representing main themes] - [Color scheme and mood description] - [Typography requirements] - [Style guidelines: modern/classic, minimal/detailed] - Aspect ratio: 2:3 (standard book cover) ``` **Chapter Sketch Prompt Structure:** ``` [Description of scene or symbol from chapter]. Style: Black and white pencil sketch, hand-drawn, with shading and texture, suitable for a memoir chapter header. ``` ### Image Integration - Save generated images as PNG files (300 DPI for print) - Place images at chapter beginnings (approx. 3-4 inches wide) - Add descriptive captions when appropriate - Ensure consistent style across all illustrations - Optimize file sizes for web and print versions ## Phase 4: PDF Conversion ### WeasyPrint Conversion ```python from weasyprint import HTML # Basic conversion HTML('manuscript.html').write_pdf('memoir.pdf') # With custom CSS for print-specific styling HTML('manuscript.html', stylesheets=['print.css']).write_pdf('memoir.pdf') # With additional options HTML( 'manuscript.html', stylesheets=['style.css', 'print.css'], url_fetcher=my_url_fetcher # For handling local image paths ).write_pdf( 'memoir.pdf', zoom=1.0, # Adjust as needed image_resolution=300 # DPI for images ) ``` ### Alternative Methods 1. **Browser Print**: Open HTML in browser and use "Print to PDF" 2. **wkhtmltopdf**: Command-line tool for batch processing ```bash wkhtmltopdf book.html book.pdf ``` 3. **Pandoc**: Universal document converter ```bash pandoc book.html -o book.pdf ``` 4. **PrinceXML**: Commercial alternative with excellent CSS support ```bash prince book.html -o book.pdf ``` ### Print-Ready Settings - **Bleeds**: 0.125 inches (if required by printer) - **Resolution**: 300 DPI for images - **Color Profile**: CMYK for professional printing - **Fonts**: Embed all fonts or use web-safe alternatives - **Accessibility**: Add semantic HTML structure for screen readers ## Phase 5: Quality Assurance ### Content Verification Checklist - [ ] All chapters present and in correct order - [ ] Transitions are meaningful and well-placed - [ ] Images match chapter content and are properly positioned - [ ] Page numbers correct and consistent throughout - [ ] Table of contents matches chapter pages - [ ] Front matter properly formatted and in correct order - [ ] Copyright and ISBN information included - [ ] Back matter complete (epilogue, author bio, etc.) - [ ] New material does not duplicate stories already present in the manuscript - [ ] New subsections appear in the intended chronological location after insertion - [ ] Rewritten additions preserve original facts and characters while improving prose style ### Technical Checks - [ ] PDF renders correctly on multiple devices and PDF readers - [ ] Fonts display properly (embedded/embeddable) - [ ] Images are high resolution (300 DPI) and clear - [ ] Margins are correct for chosen printer specifications - [ ] No text is cut off or obscured by images - [ ] Hyperlinks work correctly (if digital version) - [ ] File size appropriate for distribution method ### Proofreading - [ ] Spelling and grammar checked using multiple tools - [ ] Punctuation consistent throughout document - [ ] Capitalization follows style guide - [ ] Chapter titles match across all instances - [ ] Page breaks occur at appropriate locations - [ ] No widows/orphans in text blocks - [ ] Consistent use of italics/bold for emphasis ### Final Publication Polish Pass Do one explicit last pass after the main edit/build cycle and before delivery. **Purpose:** catch the subtle issues that survive normal proofreading — chronology drift after late insertions, duplicate story beats after memoir merging, empty subsection headings, dangling production notes, TOC/page-number drift, and small wording inconsistencies introduced during rebuilds. **Workflow:** 1. **Freeze structure first** — avoid adding new stories or changing TOC styling during this pass unless absolutely necessary. 2. **Audit for duplication and chronology drift** — confirm newly merged material adds unique information rather than repeating existing scenes. 3. **Run a style and grammar sweep** — fix lingering punctuation, capitalization, hyphenation, POV slips, and awkward repeated phrasing. 4. **Check print artifacts** — remove leftover placeholders, empty headings, editor notes, stray "end of manuscript" lines, and layout debris. 5. **Verify TOC stability** — if the TOC includes exact page numbers, calculate them from the near-final PDF after TOC styling is already frozen. If the TOC changes length again, recalculate. 6. **Spot-check chapter openings and image placement** — ensure each chapter starts cleanly, the correct sketch is attached, and no image has migrated into front matter or the TOC. 7. **Rebuild once more** — generate the final HTML/PDF pair and do a last spot-check of front matter, TOC pages, chapter numbering, and back matter. **Required outputs of the polish pass:** - Clean final HTML source - Final print-ready PDF - Rebuilt TOC reflecting the actual chapter order - Short note of any unresolved pagination caveats if TOC numbers cannot be frozen exactly in the current pipeline **Common fixes in this pass:** - Converting accidental first-person slips back to Bob-centric narration - Harmonizing names, dates, bases, institutions, and family references - Removing duplicate headings/subsections created during merges - Fixing nested TOC indentation and dot leaders - Removing leftover production text or scaffolding - Correcting chapter-image mismatches after late image swaps ## Phase 6: Delivery ### File Preparation - **Print PDF**: High-resolution, CMYK color profile, proper bleeds - **Ebook PDF**: Optimized for screen reading, smaller file size - **Source Files**: HTML, CSS, and Markdown originals - **Image Files**: Original AI-generated images and optimized versions - **Cover Files**: Print-ready cover with spine and back cover ### Distribution Methods 1. **Direct Download**: Provide zip file with all assets 2. **Cloud Storage**: Upload to Google Drive, Dropbox, etc. 3. **Print Service**: Upload directly to print-on-demand service 4. **Email**: Send files to publisher or printer 5. **Website**: Host on author website for download ### Platform-Specific Requirements - **Amazon KDP**: Specific file formats and bleed settings - **IngramSpark**: PDF/X-1a compliance for professional printing - **Local Printer**: Custom specifications as needed - **Ebook Platforms**: EPUB/MOBI formats if needed ## Tools & Technologies ### Required Tools - **Text Editor**: VS Code, Sublime Text, or similar - **HTML/CSS**: Basic knowledge for formatting - **Python**: For automation scripts (optional but helpful) - **WeasyPrint**: PDF conversion library (preferred) - **Image Generation API**: OpenRouter or similar - **Web Browser**: For testing and PDF printing ### Optional Tools - **Git**: Version control for manuscript iterations - **Pandoc**: Format conversion between document types - **Calibre**: Ebook management and conversion - **Adobe Acrobat**: Advanced PDF editing and checking - **Photoshop/GIMP**: Image editing if needed ## Best Practices ### Content Creation - Write transitions that connect emotionally with readers - Use historical events to provide context, not overwhelm - Balance personal stories with broader themes - Show, don't tell - use sensory details and specific examples - Maintain consistent voice throughout the memoir ### Technical Implementation - Test PDF conversion early and often with sample chapters - Keep original AI prompts for future image regeneration - Maintain version control for all manuscript iterations - Create backup copies of all generated files - Document any custom formatting requirements ### Quality Control - Get feedback from beta readers before finalizing - Print a proof copy before mass production - Check color accuracy if using color images - Verify all legal requirements (copyright, ISBN, etc.) - Test accessibility features for digital versions ## Troubleshooting ### Common Issues & Solutions **Issue**: Images not generating properly **Solution**: Refine prompts with more specific details, try different AI models, adjust parameters **Issue**: PDF formatting breaks or looks wrong **Solution**: Check CSS for print-specific rules, ensure proper page breaks, validate HTML structure **Issue**: Transitions feel forced or unnatural **Solution**: Read aloud to test flow, get feedback from others, revise for natural language **Issue**: Historical details inaccurate **Solution**: Cross-reference multiple sources, consult experts if possible, add disclaimers if uncertain **Issue**: File sizes too large for distribution **Solution**: Optimize images (compress without losing quality), minimize CSS, remove unnecessary assets **Issue**: WeasyPrint not available or not working **Solution**: Use browser print method or install wkhtmltopdf as alternative **Issue**: Images not displaying in PDF **Solution**: Check file paths, ensure images are accessible, use absolute paths if needed ## Success Metrics - **Content Quality**: Positive feedback from beta readers and reviewers - **Technical Quality**: Professional appearance, no formatting errors - **Production Readiness**: Files accepted by print-on-demand services - # OpenClaw Hermes

## Overview

Use this skill to help authors prepare a book for publication across major self-publishing retailers and promotion channels. Treat the workflow as a compliance-first launch review: verify rights, files, metadata, AI disclosure, ISBN decisions, retailer rules, live links, and promotion readiness.

This skill is not legal advice. When legal risk is material, state the risk plainly and recommend professional legal review.

## Core Workflow

1. Identify the target path:
   - Kindle only: use Amazon KDP checks.
   - Wide eBook: use KDP without KDP Select plus Kobo, Barnes and Noble, and Google Play checks.
   - Print: add print ISBN, trim, cover, barcode, and PDF checks.
   - Promotion: add Book Barbarian readiness checks.

2. Build a master metadata record:
   - title, subtitle, series, author, contributors, publisher, description, categories, keywords, language, publication date, territories, prices, ISBNs, AI-use record, retailer links.

3. Run the universal compliance gates before retailer-specific checks:
   - rights and ownership
   - manuscript quality
   - cover quality
   - metadata consistency
   - ISBN plan
   - AI content disclosure
   - adult/sensitive content classification
   - pricing and territorial rights

4. Run retailer-specific checks using the references:
   - Amazon KDP: see references/kdp.md
   - Kobo Writing Life: see references/kobo.md
   - Barnes and Noble Press: see references/barnes-noble.md
   - Google Play Books: see references/google-play.md
   - Book Barbarian: see references/book-barbarian.md
   - Official links: see references/official-links.md

5. Output a decision:
   - Pass: ready to publish or submit.
   - Fix: clear blocker exists.
   - Risk: not blocked, but needs judgment or legal/policy review.

## Universal Compliance Gates

Always check these before recommending publication.

### Rights

### Metadata

Title, subtitle, author, and series details must match the cover and manuscript title page. Do not allow keyword stuffing, competitor names, temporary price claims, fake awards, misleading categories, or Amazon-specific language on non-Amazon retailers.

Use one ISBN per format: eBook, paperback, hardcover, audiobook. Retailer-provided free ISBNs normally stay tied to that retailer. For serious wide publishing, recommend publisher-owned ISBNs from the official ISBN agency for the user's country.

For Amazon KDP, disclose final reader-facing AI-generated text, images, or translations. AI-assisted brainstorming, outlining, editing, proofreading, and refinement do not require KDP disclosure when final content is human-created. {"success": true, "name": "memoir-publishing-workflow", "description": "Comprehensive approach for transforming raw memoirs into professionally formatted books with enhanced transitions, proper publishing details, and AI integration.", "tags": ["memoir", "publishing", "formatting", "transitions", "PDF", "HTML", "WeasyPrint", "OpenRouter", "AI-generation", "image-creation"], "related_skills": [], "content": "--- name: memoir-publishing-workflow version: 2.1.0 description: Comprehensive approach for transforming raw memoirs into professionally formatted books with enhanced transitions, proper publishing details, and AI integration. tags: [memoir, publishing, formatting, transitions, PDF, HTML, WeasyPrint, OpenRouter, AI-generation, image-creation] depends: [add_transitions_to_unwritten_future, manuscript-conversion-pipeline, manuscript-restructuring] --- # Memoir & Book Saga Publishing Pipeline ## Overview A high-production pipeline for multi-volume book series and memoirs, integrating cinematic AI-generated cover art, systematic front/back matter assembly, and professional PDF generation using ReportLab as a robust alternative to Pandoc. ## When to Use - Building professional-quality books or series for digital delivery. - When Pandoc or complex LaTeX environments are unavailable and a Python-native solution is needed. - Requiring consistent visual branding across a series (covers, typography). ## Workflow Steps ### 1. Visual Branding (Covers) - **Tooling:** Use `requests` with endpoints like `pollinations.ai` for reliable, no-key fallback image generation. - **Prompts:** Use cinematic descriptors ("hyper-realistic", "high contrast", "light band for title space") to ensure professional quality. - **Aspect Ratio:** Standard 2:3 portrait (1024x1536) for book covers. ### 2. Front & Back Matter - **Title Page:** Enshrine title, subtitle, author, and specific taglines. - **Copyright:** Include Standard placeholders: Year, Publisher, Rights Reserved note. - **Author Note:** Include a specific "Note on composition" or "AI Disclaimer" if assisted by agents. - **Back Cover:** Include praise placeholders, author bio, and standard identifiers (ISBN/Logo placeholders). ### 3. Professional PDF Generation (ReportLab) Since `pandoc` often fails due to complex dependencies or missing PDF engines, use a direct `ReportLab` implementation for total layout control: - **Margins:** 2.5cm standard for A4. - **Typography:** Use `Times-Roman` (12pt Body) and `Times-Bold` (18pt Headings) for the "bestseller" look. - **Justification:** Set `alignment=4` in `ParagraphStyle` for professional blocks. - **Dynamic TOC:** - Scan the manuscript for `## Chapter` headers. - Build a list of `Paragraph` items in the `story`. - **Media Delivery:** Always provide an absolute path for the final PDF to ensure `MEDIA:/path` works on Telegram. ## Example ReportLab Implementation ```python from reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak, Image from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4 from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet, ParagraphStyle from reportlab.lib.units import cm def build_book(md_path, cover_path, output_pdf): doc = SimpleDocTemplate(output_pdf, pagesize=A4, margins=2.5*cm) styles = getSampleStyleSheet() story = [Image(cover_path, width=16*cm, height=24*cm), PageBreak()] # ... logic to parse markdown and append PageBreaks at ## Chapter doc.build(story) ``` **Skill for:** Systematically transforming a raw memoir manuscript into a professionally formatted, published-quality book (HTML/PDF) with enhanced transitions, proper front/back matter, AI-generated images, and print-ready output. ## Overview This skill provides a comprehensive approach for converting raw memoir content into a print-ready format, including: - **Manuscript preparation** - Content review, editing, and structural organization - **Formatting & layout** - HTML/CSS styling for professional appearance - **Image generation** - AI-created chapter illustrations and cover art - **PDF conversion** - Multiple methods for print-ready output - **Quality assurance** - Verification and testing procedures - **Final publication polish** - Late-stage cleanup, exact pagination checks, and narrative consistency verification - **Delivery** - File preparation and distribution The workflow combines traditional publishing techniques with modern AI tools to create high-quality books efficiently. ## When to Use - When preparing a memoir for publication - When enhancing narrative flow with historical context - When formatting books for print or digital distribution - When working with limited formatting tools - When creating professional-quality books without expensive software ## Prerequisites - Raw manuscript content (Markdown or text format) - Basic understanding of book structure (front matter, chapters, back matter) - Access to image generation tools (OpenRouter recommended) - PDF conversion capability (WeasyPrint preferred, alternatives available) - Python environment for automation (optional but helpful) ## Phase 1: Manuscript Preparation ### Content Review Process 1. **Read through complete manuscript** to understand narrative flow and identify gaps 2. **Check for consistency** in voice, tense, and perspective throughout 3. **Verify historical facts** and timeline accuracy 4. **Evaluate transition quality** between chapters and parts 5. **Assess emotional impact** and reader engagement ### Editing Approach - **Structural editing**: Ensure logical chapter progression and proper sequencing - **Line editing**: Improve sentence flow, readability, and style - **Transition enhancement**: Replace placeholders with rich, personal reflections - **Fact-checking**: Verify historical events and personal details - **Sensitivity review**: Ensure respectful representation of all people and events - **Deduplication-first memoir merging**: When new story fragments arrive after a manuscript already exists, first audit the current manuscript to determine what is already present, what is only partially represented, and what is truly new. Merge only unique facts or sharper details; do not duplicate full stories already in the book. - **Insertion by narrative anchor**: In long HTML memoirs, avoid naive before/after-heading insertion when using BeautifulSoup or similar parsers. Anchoring directly on heading tags can accidentally reorder content. Instead, insert new subsections after the final paragraph of the intended logical block, then verify local ordering with spot reads. - **BeautifulSoup ordering pitfall**: In very large HTML files, repeated `insert_before` / `insert_after` operations with parsed fragments can still produce unexpected heading/paragraph order if you anchor on the wrong node or iterate over fragment children naively. Safer patterns are: (1) insert after the last paragraph of the target block, not the heading; (2) use a temporary marker/comment anchor; and (3) immediately verify the edited region with `read_file` around the insertion point before making more edits. - **Chapter reordering after expansion**: When chronology changes late in the process, reorder whole `
` blocks rather than trying to renumber content in place. After moving sections, regenerate the Table of Contents directly from the actual chapter order in the HTML so the TOC cannot drift from the manuscript structure. - **TOC pagination stabilization for print HTML/PDF**: In WeasyPrint-style book pipelines, a multi-page TOC can change later page numbers every time it is edited, because the TOC itself shifts the front matter length. The reliable workflow is: (1) clean up TOC layout first (dot leaders, indentation, continuation pages), (2) generate a PDF and extract actual chapter/subsection start pages, (3) write those numbers back into the TOC, and (4) avoid further TOC layout edits unless you are prepared to recompute all page numbers again. If exact publication page numbers matter, freeze TOC styling before the final mapping pass. - **TOC extraction false-positive pitfall**: When page numbers are extracted from PDF text, searching for a chapter title from page 1 can incorrectly match the TOC page instead of the real chapter page. A more reliable method is to insert hidden locator strings such as `CHAPTER_START_01` / `PART_START_01` into the body HTML, detect the first actual body page in the PDF, and only search for markers from that page forward. This prevents chapter-page mappings from collapsing onto TOC pages during automated rebuilds. - **Late-pass image replacement workflow**: For targeted chapter-image swaps in large final HTML files, replace only the relevant `` `src` attributes by chapter title, rebuild the PDF, then verify page count and title metadata. This is safer than regenerating the entire manuscript from earlier passes. - **Transition expansion workflow**: When asked to make transitions longer, treat them as miniature narrative essays rather than filler. Each should (a) begin from the emotional residue of the prior chapter, (b) explain what was happening historically in the wider world at that time, (c) connect that history back to Bob's lived experience in plain human language, and (d) point naturally toward the next chapter. In practice, ~2.5K–3K characters per transition can work well for a rich but readable bridge in HTML memoir format. - **Image-generation environment reality check**: Do not assume image API access is available just because Hermes config references OpenRouter or a vision model. Check the live environment first. If external image generation is unavailable, update the chapter prompt files anyway and either (a) produce temporary local sketch placeholders, clearly labeled as such, or (b) finish the manuscript/PDF and defer true regeneration to a follow-up pass. - **Telegram delivery fallback**: If direct `send_message(target='telegram')` fails because no Telegram home channel is configured, deliver book files in the assistant response using `MEDIA:/absolute/path` instead of stopping the workflow. - **Late-stage cleanup audit**: Before finalizing an expanded memoir, run a targeted audit for repeated story beats, duplicated exposition, chronology drift, and empty or near-empty subsection headings. Large embedded-image HTML files are too heavy to inspect casually; sample by chapter/region and, when useful, delegate a focused audit that returns exact subsection names to cut, merge, or move. - **Transition expansion standard**: For this style of memoir, transitions should often be several dense paragraphs rather than brief connectors. Humanize them by tying private emotional movement to the larger historical atmosphere of the period (Cold War anxiety, postwar prosperity, technology acceleration, etc.), but do not let them invent personal facts. - **Graceful degradation when image regeneration is blocked**: If the manuscript needs updated chapter sketches but image-generation credentials are unavailable in the active execution environment, still complete the editorial and print-ready pass. Refresh all image prompt files, preserve existing images, note the limitation clearly, and defer only the actual regeneration step. ### Key Deliverables - Clean, edited manuscript file (Markdown format) - Chapter-by-chapter analysis report - Transition quality assessment - Historical context verification - Sensitivity review notes ## Phase 2: Formatting & Layout ### HTML Structure ```html Memoir Title

``` ### CSS Styling Specifications ```css /* Base styles */ body { font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; margin: 2.5cm; /* Standard print margins */ line-height: 1.5; color: #333; max-width: 100%; hyphens: auto; } /* Page setup for A4 */ @page { size: A4; margin: 2.5cm; } /* Chapter headings */ .chapter { page-break-before: always; margin-top: 3cm; } .chapter-number { font-size: 2em; font-weight: bold; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.1em; margin-bottom: 0.5em; } .chapter-title { font-size: 1.5em; font-weight: normal; margin-bottom: 1em; } /* Transitions */ .transition { font-style: italic; margin: 2em 0; padding: 1em 2em; border-left: 3px solid #ccc; background: #f9f9f9; } /* Page numbers */ @bottom-center { content: counter(page); font-size: 0.9em; color: #666; } /* Headers */ @top-left { content: "The Future is Unwritten"; font-size: 0.8em; color: #999; } @top-right { content: "Robert Mills"; font-size: 0.8em; color: #999; } ``` ### Special Elements - **Transitions**: 10-20 sentence passages between chapters - **Historical context**: Integrated seamlessly into narrative - **Physiological effects**: Described in accessible, engaging language - **Images**: Placeholder positions with captions - **Drop caps**: First letter of each chapter enlarged and styled - **Part openings**: Special formatting for major section divisions ## Phase 3: Image Generation ### Image Types Required 1. **Cover Image** - Professional, eye-catching design 2. **Chapter Illustrations** - One per chapter (black and white sketches) 3. **Epilogue Image** - Reflective closing image ### Prompt Engineering Approach For each image, create specific prompts based on chapter content: **Cover Prompt Structure:** ``` Create a professional book cover for the memoir "[TITLE]" by [AUTHOR]. The cover should feature: - [Key visual elements representing main themes] - [Color scheme and mood description] - [Typography requirements] - [Style guidelines: modern/classic, minimal/detailed] - Aspect ratio: 2:3 (standard book cover) ``` **Chapter Sketch Prompt Structure:** ``` [Description of scene or symbol from chapter]. Style: Black and white pencil sketch, hand-drawn, with shading and texture, suitable for a memoir chapter header. ``` ### Image Integration - Save generated images as PNG files (300 DPI for print) - Place images at chapter beginnings (approx. 3-4 inches wide) - Add descriptive captions when appropriate - Ensure consistent style across all illustrations - Optimize file sizes for web and print versions ## Phase 4: PDF Conversion ### WeasyPrint Conversion ```python from weasyprint import HTML # Basic conversion HTML('manuscript.html').write_pdf('memoir.pdf') # With custom CSS for print-specific styling HTML('manuscript.html', stylesheets=['print.css']).write_pdf('memoir.pdf') # With additional options HTML( 'manuscript.html', stylesheets=['style.css', 'print.css'], url_fetcher=my_url_fetcher # For handling local image paths ).write_pdf( 'memoir.pdf', zoom=1.0, # Adjust as needed image_resolution=300 # DPI for images ) ``` ### Alternative Methods 1. **Browser Print**: Open HTML in browser and use "Print to PDF" 2. **wkhtmltopdf**: Command-line tool for batch processing ```bash wkhtmltopdf book.html book.pdf ``` 3. **Pandoc**: Universal document converter ```bash pandoc book.html -o book.pdf ``` 4. **PrinceXML**: Commercial alternative with excellent CSS support ```bash prince book.html -o book.pdf ``` ### Print-Ready Settings - **Bleeds**: 0.125 inches (if required by printer) - **Resolution**: 300 DPI for images - **Color Profile**: CMYK for professional printing - **Fonts**: Embed all fonts or use web-safe alternatives - **Accessibility**: Add semantic HTML structure for screen readers ## Phase 5: Quality Assurance ### Content Verification Checklist - [ ] All chapters present and in correct order - [ ] Transitions are meaningful and well-placed - [ ] Images match chapter content and are properly positioned - [ ] Page numbers correct and consistent throughout - [ ] Table of contents matches chapter pages - [ ] Front matter properly formatted and in correct order - [ ] Copyright and ISBN information included - [ ] Back matter complete (epilogue, author bio, etc.) - [ ] New material does not duplicate stories already present in the manuscript - [ ] New subsections appear in the intended chronological location after insertion - [ ] Rewritten additions preserve original facts and characters while improving prose style ### Technical Checks - [ ] PDF renders correctly on multiple devices and PDF readers - [ ] Fonts display properly (embedded/embeddable) - [ ] Images are high resolution (300 DPI) and clear - [ ] Margins are correct for chosen printer specifications - [ ] No text is cut off or obscured by images - [ ] Hyperlinks work correctly (if digital version) - [ ] File size appropriate for distribution method ### Proofreading - [ ] Spelling and grammar checked using multiple tools - [ ] Punctuation consistent throughout document - [ ] Capitalization follows style guide - [ ] Chapter titles match across all instances - [ ] Page breaks occur at appropriate locations - [ ] No widows/orphans in text blocks - [ ] Consistent use of italics/bold for emphasis ### Final Publication Polish Pass Do one explicit last pass after the main edit/build cycle and before delivery. **Purpose:** catch the subtle issues that survive normal proofreading — chronology drift after late insertions, duplicate story beats after memoir merging, empty subsection headings, dangling production notes, TOC/page-number drift, and small wording inconsistencies introduced during rebuilds. **Workflow:** 1. **Freeze structure first** — avoid adding new stories or changing TOC styling during this pass unless absolutely necessary. 2. **Audit for duplication and chronology drift** — confirm newly merged material adds unique information rather than repeating existing scenes. 3. **Run a style and grammar sweep** — fix lingering punctuation, capitalization, hyphenation, POV slips, and awkward repeated phrasing. 4. **Check print artifacts** — remove leftover placeholders, empty headings, editor notes, stray "end of manuscript" lines, and layout debris. 5. **Verify TOC stability** — if the TOC includes exact page numbers, calculate them from the near-final PDF after TOC styling is already frozen. If the TOC changes length again, recalculate. 6. **Spot-check chapter openings and image placement** — ensure each chapter starts cleanly, the correct sketch is attached, and no image has migrated into front matter or the TOC. 7. **Rebuild once more** — generate the final HTML/PDF pair and do a last spot-check of front matter, TOC pages, chapter numbering, and back matter. **Required outputs of the polish pass:** - Clean final HTML source - Final print-ready PDF - Rebuilt TOC reflecting the actual chapter order - Short note of any unresolved pagination caveats if TOC numbers cannot be frozen exactly in the current pipeline **Common fixes in this pass:** - Converting accidental first-person slips back to Bob-centric narration - Harmonizing names, dates, bases, institutions, and family references - Removing duplicate headings/subsections created during merges - Fixing nested TOC indentation and dot leaders - Removing leftover production text or scaffolding - Correcting chapter-image mismatches after late image swaps ## Phase 6: Delivery ### File Preparation - **Print PDF**: High-resolution, CMYK color profile, proper bleeds - **Ebook PDF**: Optimized for screen reading, smaller file size - **Source Files**: HTML, CSS, and Markdown originals - **Image Files**: Original AI-generated images and optimized versions - **Cover Files**: Print-ready cover with spine and back cover ### Distribution Methods 1. **Direct Download**: Provide zip file with all assets 2. **Cloud Storage**: Upload to Google Drive, Dropbox, etc. 3. **Print Service**: Upload directly to print-on-demand service 4. **Email**: Send files to publisher or printer 5. **Website**: Host on author website for download ### Platform-Specific Requirements - **Amazon KDP**: Specific file formats and bleed settings - **IngramSpark**: PDF/X-1a compliance for professional printing - **Local Printer**: Custom specifications as needed - **Ebook Platforms**: EPUB/MOBI formats if needed ## Tools & Technologies ### Required Tools - **Text Editor**: VS Code, Sublime Text, or similar - **HTML/CSS**: Basic knowledge for formatting - **Python**: For automation scripts (optional but helpful) - **WeasyPrint**: PDF conversion library (preferred) - **Image Generation API**: OpenRouter or similar - **Web Browser**: For testing and PDF printing ### Optional Tools - **Git**: Version control for manuscript iterations - **Pandoc**: Format conversion between document types - **Calibre**: Ebook management and conversion - **Adobe Acrobat**: Advanced PDF editing and checking - **Photoshop/GIMP**: Image editing if needed ## Best Practices ### Content Creation - Write transitions that connect emotionally with readers - Use historical events to provide context, not overwhelm - Balance personal stories with broader themes - Show, don't tell - use sensory details and specific examples - Maintain consistent voice throughout the memoir ### Technical Implementation - Test PDF conversion early and often with sample chapters - Keep original AI prompts for future image regeneration - Maintain version control for all manuscript iterations - Create backup copies of all generated files - Document any custom formatting requirements ### Quality Control - Get feedback from beta readers before finalizing - Print a proof copy before mass production - Check color accuracy if using color images - Verify all legal requirements (copyright, ISBN, etc.) - Test accessibility features for digital versions ## Troubleshooting ### Common Issues & Solutions **Issue**: Images not generating properly **Solution**: Refine prompts with more specific details, try different AI models, adjust parameters **Issue**: PDF formatting breaks or looks wrong **Solution**: Check CSS for print-specific rules, ensure proper page breaks, validate HTML structure **Issue**: Transitions feel forced or unnatural **Solution**: Read aloud to test flow, get feedback from others, revise for natural language **Issue**: Historical details inaccurate **Solution**: Cross-reference multiple sources, consult experts if possible, add disclaimers if uncertain **Issue**: File sizes too large for distribution **Solution**: Optimize images (compress without losing quality), minimize CSS, remove unnecessary assets **Issue**: WeasyPrint not available or not working **Solution**: Use browser print method or install wkhtmltopdf as alternative **Issue**: Images not displaying in PDF **Solution**: Check file paths, ensure images are accessible, use absolute paths if needed ## Success Metrics - **Content Quality**: Positive feedback from beta readers and reviewers - **Technical Quality**: Professional appearance, no formatting errors - **Production Readiness**: Files accepted by print-on-demand services - **Reader Engagement**: Strong reviews, good sales performance - **Personal Satisfaction**: Author feels accurately represented ## Example Project Structure ``` memoir-project/ ├── manuscript/ │ ├── raw/ # Original content │ ├── edited/ # Edited manuscript │ └── final.md # Final Markdown ├── formatting/ │ ├── html/ # HTML files │ ├── css/ # CSS stylesheets │ └── templates/ # Layout templates ├── images/ │ ├── generated/ # AI-generated images │ ├── placeholders/ # Temporary placeholders │ └── final/ # Optimized images ├── pdf/ │ ├── drafts/ # Test PDFs │ ├── proofs/ # Proof copies │ └── final/ # Production PDFs ├── scripts/ # Automation scripts ├── docs/ # Documentation └── README.md # Project overview ``` ## Notes This workflow combines traditional publishing approaches with modern AI tools. {"success": true, "name": "memoir-publishing-workflow", "description": "Comprehensive approach for transforming raw memoirs into professionally formatted books with enhanced transitions, proper publishing details, and AI integration.", "tags": ["memoir", "publishing", "formatting", "transitions", "PDF", "HTML", "WeasyPrint", "OpenRouter", "AI-generation", "image-creation"], "related_skills": [], "content": "--- name: memoir-publishing-workflow version: 2.1.0 description: Comprehensive approach for transforming raw memoirs into professionally formatted books with enhanced transitions, proper publishing details, and AI integration. tags: [memoir, publishing, formatting, transitions, PDF, HTML, WeasyPrint, OpenRouter, AI-generation, image-creation] depends: [add_transitions_to_unwritten_future, manuscript-conversion-pipeline, manuscript-restructuring] --- # Memoir & Book Saga Publishing Pipeline ## Overview A high-production pipeline for multi-volume book series and memoirs, integrating cinematic AI-generated cover art, systematic front/back matter assembly, and professional PDF generation using ReportLab as a robust alternative to Pandoc. ## When to Use - Building professional-quality books or series for digital delivery. - When Pandoc or complex LaTeX environments are unavailable and a Python-native solution is needed. - Requiring consistent visual branding across a series (covers, typography). ## Workflow Steps ### 1. Visual Branding (Covers) - **Tooling:** Use `requests` with endpoints like `pollinations.ai` for reliable, no-key fallback image generation. - **Prompts:** Use cinematic descriptors ("hyper-realistic", "high contrast", "light band for title space") to ensure professional quality. - **Aspect Ratio:** Standard 2:3 portrait (1024x1536) for book covers. ### 2. Front & Back Matter - **Title Page:** Enshrine title, subtitle, author, and specific taglines. - **Copyright:** Include Standard placeholders: Year, Publisher, Rights Reserved note. - **Author Note:** Include a specific "Note on composition" or "AI Disclaimer" if assisted by agents. - **Back Cover:** Include praise placeholders, author bio, and standard identifiers (ISBN/Logo placeholders). ### 3. Professional PDF Generation (ReportLab) Since `pandoc` often fails due to complex dependencies or missing PDF engines, use a direct `ReportLab` implementation for total layout control: - **Margins:** 2.5cm standard for A4. - **Typography:** Use `Times-Roman` (12pt Body) and `Times-Bold` (18pt Headings) for the "bestseller" look. - **Justification:** Set `alignment=4` in `ParagraphStyle` for professional blocks. - **Dynamic TOC:** - Scan the manuscript for `## Chapter` headers. - Build a list of `Paragraph` items in the `story`. - **Media Delivery:** Always provide an absolute path for the final PDF to ensure `MEDIA:/path` works on Telegram. ## Example ReportLab Implementation ```python from reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak, Image from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4 from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet, ParagraphStyle from reportlab.lib.units import cm def build_book(md_path, cover_path, output_pdf): doc = SimpleDocTemplate(output_pdf, pagesize=A4, margins=2.5*cm) styles = getSampleStyleSheet() story = [Image(cover_path, width=16*cm, height=24*cm), PageBreak()] # ... logic to parse markdown and append PageBreaks at ## Chapter doc.build(story) ``` **Skill for:** Systematically transforming a raw memoir manuscript into a professionally formatted, published-quality book (HTML/PDF) with enhanced transitions, proper front/back matter, AI-generated images, and print-ready output. ## Overview This skill provides a comprehensive approach for converting raw memoir content into a print-ready format, including: - **Manuscript preparation** - Content review, editing, and structural organization - **Formatting & layout** - HTML/CSS styling for professional appearance - **Image generation** - AI-created chapter illustrations and cover art - **PDF conversion** - Multiple methods for print-ready output - **Quality assurance** - Verification and testing procedures - **Final publication polish** - Late-stage cleanup, exact pagination checks, and narrative consistency verification - **Delivery** - File preparation and distribution The workflow combines traditional publishing techniques with modern AI tools to create high-quality books efficiently. ## When to Use - When preparing a memoir for publication - When enhancing narrative flow with historical context - When formatting books for print or digital distribution - When working with limited formatting tools - When creating professional-quality books without expensive software ## Prerequisites - Raw manuscript content (Markdown or text format) - Basic understanding of book structure (front matter, chapters, back matter) - Access to image generation tools (OpenRouter recommended) - PDF conversion capability (WeasyPrint preferred, alternatives available) - Python environment for automation (optional but helpful) ## Phase 1: Manuscript Preparation ### Content Review Process 1. **Read through complete manuscript** to understand narrative flow and identify gaps 2. **Check for consistency** in voice, tense, and perspective throughout 3. **Verify historical facts** and timeline accuracy 4. **Evaluate transition quality** between chapters and parts 5. **Assess emotional impact** and reader engagement ### Editing Approach - **Structural editing**: Ensure logical chapter progression and proper sequencing - **Line editing**: Improve sentence flow, readability, and style - **Transition enhancement**: Replace placeholders with rich, personal reflections - **Fact-checking**: Verify historical events and personal details - **Sensitivity review**: Ensure respectful representation of all people and events - **Deduplication-first memoir merging**: When new story fragments arrive after a manuscript already exists, first audit the current manuscript to determine what is already present, what is only partially represented, and what is truly new. Merge only unique facts or sharper details; do not duplicate full stories already in the book. - **Insertion by narrative anchor**: In long HTML memoirs, avoid naive before/after-heading insertion when using BeautifulSoup or similar parsers. Anchoring directly on heading tags can accidentally reorder content. Instead, insert new subsections after the final paragraph of the intended logical block, then verify local ordering with spot reads. - **BeautifulSoup ordering pitfall**: In very large HTML files, repeated `insert_before` / `insert_after` operations with parsed fragments can still produce unexpected heading/paragraph order if you anchor on the wrong node or iterate over fragment children naively. Safer patterns are: (1) insert after the last paragraph of the target block, not the heading; (2) use a temporary marker/comment anchor; and (3) immediately verify the edited region with `read_file` around the insertion point before making more edits. - **Chapter reordering after expansion**: When chronology changes late in the process, reorder whole `
` blocks rather than trying to renumber content in place. After moving sections, regenerate the Table of Contents directly from the actual chapter order in the HTML so the TOC cannot drift from the manuscript structure. - **TOC pagination stabilization for print HTML/PDF**: In WeasyPrint-style book pipelines, a multi-page TOC can change later page numbers every time it is edited, because the TOC itself shifts the front matter length. The reliable workflow is: (1) clean up TOC layout first (dot leaders, indentation, continuation pages), (2) generate a PDF and extract actual chapter/subsection start pages, (3) write those numbers back into the TOC, and (4) avoid further TOC layout edits unless you are prepared to recompute all page numbers again. If exact publication page numbers matter, freeze TOC styling before the final mapping pass. - **TOC extraction false-positive pitfall**: When page numbers are extracted from PDF text, searching for a chapter title from page 1 can incorrectly match the TOC page instead of the real chapter page. A more reliable method is to insert hidden locator strings such as `CHAPTER_START_01` / `PART_START_01` into the body HTML, detect the first actual body page in the PDF, and only search for markers from that page forward. This prevents chapter-page mappings from collapsing onto TOC pages during automated rebuilds. - **Late-pass image replacement workflow**: For targeted chapter-image swaps in large final HTML files, replace only the relevant `` `src` attributes by chapter title, rebuild the PDF, then verify page count and title metadata. This is safer than regenerating the entire manuscript from earlier passes. - **Transition expansion workflow**: When asked to make transitions longer, treat them as miniature narrative essays rather than filler. Each should (a) begin from the emotional residue of the prior chapter, (b) explain what was happening historically in the wider world at that time, (c) connect that history back to Bob's lived experience in plain human language, and (d) point naturally toward the next chapter. In practice, ~2.5K–3K characters per transition can work well for a rich but readable bridge in HTML memoir format. - **Image-generation environment reality check**: Do not assume image API access is available just because Hermes config references OpenRouter or a vision model. Check the live environment first. If external image generation is unavailable, update the chapter prompt files anyway and either (a) produce temporary local sketch placeholders, clearly labeled as such, or (b) finish the manuscript/PDF and defer true regeneration to a follow-up pass. - **Telegram delivery fallback**: If direct `send_message(target='telegram')` fails because no Telegram home channel is configured, deliver book files in the assistant response using `MEDIA:/absolute/path` instead of stopping the workflow. - **Late-stage cleanup audit**: Before finalizing an expanded memoir, run a targeted audit for repeated story beats, duplicated exposition, chronology drift, and empty or near-empty subsection headings. Large embedded-image HTML files are too heavy to inspect casually; sample by chapter/region and, when useful, delegate a focused audit that returns exact subsection names to cut, merge, or move. - **Transition expansion standard**: For this style of memoir, transitions should often be several dense paragraphs rather than brief connectors. Humanize them by tying private emotional movement to the larger historical atmosphere of the period (Cold War anxiety, postwar prosperity, technology acceleration, etc.), but do not let them invent personal facts. - **Graceful degradation when image regeneration is blocked**: If the manuscript needs updated chapter sketches but image-generation credentials are unavailable in the active execution environment, still complete the editorial and print-ready pass. Refresh all image prompt files, preserve existing images, note the limitation clearly, and defer only the actual regeneration step. ### Key Deliverables - Clean, edited manuscript file (Markdown format) - Chapter-by-chapter analysis report - Transition quality assessment - Historical context verification - Sensitivity review notes ## Phase 2: Formatting & Layout ### HTML Structure ```html Memoir Title

{"success": true, "name": "memoir-publishing-workflow", "description": "Comprehensive approach for transforming raw memoirs into professionally formatted books with enhanced transitions, proper publishing details, and AI integration.", "tags": ["memoir", "publishing", "formatting", "transitions", "PDF", "HTML", "WeasyPrint", "OpenRouter", "AI-generation", "image-creation"], "related_skills": [], "content": "--- name: memoir-publishing-workflow version: 2.1.0 description: Comprehensive approach for transforming raw memoirs into professionally formatted books with enhanced transitions, proper publishing details, and AI integration. tags: [memoir, publishing, formatting, transitions, PDF, HTML, WeasyPrint, OpenRouter, AI-generation, image-creation] depends: [add_transitions_to_unwritten_future, manuscript-conversion-pipeline, manuscript-restructuring] --- # Memoir & Book Saga Publishing Pipeline ## Overview A high-production pipeline for multi-volume book series and memoirs, integrating cinematic AI-generated cover art, systematic front/back matter assembly, and professional PDF generation using ReportLab as a robust alternative to Pandoc. ## When to Use - Building professional-quality books or series for digital delivery. - When Pandoc or complex LaTeX environments are unavailable and a Python-native solution is needed. - Requiring consistent visual branding across a series (covers, typography). ## Workflow Steps ### 1. Visual Branding (Covers) - **Tooling:** Use `requests` with endpoints like `pollinations.ai` for reliable, no-key fallback image generation. - **Prompts:** Use cinematic descriptors ("hyper-realistic", "high contrast", "light band for title space") to ensure professional quality. - **Aspect Ratio:** Standard 2:3 portrait (1024x1536) for book covers. ### 2. Front & Back Matter - **Title Page:** Enshrine title, subtitle, author, and specific taglines. - **Copyright:** Include Standard placeholders: Year, Publisher, Rights Reserved note. - **Author Note:** Include a specific "Note on composition" or "AI Disclaimer" if assisted by agents. - **Back Cover:** Include praise placeholders, author bio, and standard identifiers (ISBN/Logo placeholders). ### 3. Professional PDF Generation (ReportLab) Since `pandoc` often fails due to complex dependencies or missing PDF engines, use a direct `ReportLab` implementation for total layout control: - **Margins:** 2.5cm standard for A4. - **Typography:** Use `Times-Roman` (12pt Body) and `Times-Bold` (18pt Headings) for the "bestseller" look. - **Justification:** Set `alignment=4` in `ParagraphStyle` for professional blocks. - **Dynamic TOC:** - Scan the manuscript for `## Chapter` headers. - Build a list of `Paragraph` items in the `story`. - **Media Delivery:** Always provide an absolute path for the final PDF to ensure `MEDIA:/path` works on Telegram. ## Example ReportLab Implementation ```python from reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak, Image from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4 from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet, ParagraphStyle from reportlab.lib.units import cm def build_book(md_path, cover_path, output_pdf): doc = SimpleDocTemplate(output_pdf, pagesize=A4, margins=2.5*cm) styles = getSampleStyleSheet() story = [Image(cover_path, width=16*cm, height=24*cm), PageBreak()] # ... logic to parse markdown and append PageBreaks at ## Chapter doc.build(story) ``` **Skill for:** Systematically transforming a raw memoir manuscript into a professionally formatted, published-quality book (HTML/PDF) with enhanced transitions, proper front/back matter, AI-generated images, and print-ready output. ## Overview This skill provides a comprehensive approach for converting raw memoir content into a print-ready format, including: - **Manuscript preparation** - Content review, editing, and structural organization - **Formatting & layout** - HTML/CSS styling for professional appearance - **Image generation** - AI-created chapter illustrations and cover art - **PDF conversion** - Multiple methods for print-ready output - **Quality assurance** - Verification and testing procedures - **Final publication polish** - Late-stage cleanup, exact pagination checks, and narrative consistency verification - **Delivery** - File preparation and distribution The workflow combines traditional publishing techniques with modern AI tools to create high-quality books efficiently. ## When to Use - When preparing a memoir for publication - When enhancing narrative flow with historical context - When formatting books for print or digital distribution - When working with limited formatting tools - When creating professional-quality books without expensive software ## Prerequisites - Raw manuscript content (Markdown or text format) - Basic understanding of book structure (front matter, chapters, back matter) - Access to image generation tools (OpenRouter recommended) - PDF conversion capability (WeasyPrint preferred, alternatives available) - Python environment for automation (optional but helpful) ## Phase 1: Manuscript Preparation ### Content Review Process 1. **Read through complete manuscript** to understand narrative flow and identify gaps 2. **Check for consistency** in voice, tense, and perspective throughout 3. **Verify historical facts** and timeline accuracy 4. **Evaluate transition quality** between chapters and parts 5. **Assess emotional impact** and reader engagement ### Editing Approach - **Structural editing**: Ensure logical chapter progression and proper sequencing - **Line editing**: Improve sentence flow, readability, and style - **Transition enhancement**: Replace placeholders with rich, personal reflections - **Fact-checking**: Verify historical events and personal details - **Sensitivity review**: Ensure respectful representation of all people and events - **Deduplication-first memoir merging**: When new story fragments arrive after a manuscript already exists, first audit the current manuscript to determine what is already present, what is only partially represented, and what is truly new. Merge only unique facts or sharper details; do not duplicate full stories already in the book. - **Insertion by narrative anchor**: In long HTML memoirs, avoid naive before/after-heading insertion when using BeautifulSoup or similar parsers. Anchoring directly on heading tags can accidentally reorder content. Instead, insert new subsections after the final paragraph of the intended logical block, then verify local ordering with spot reads. - **BeautifulSoup ordering pitfall**: In very large HTML files, repeated `insert_before` / `insert_after` operations with parsed fragments can still produce unexpected heading/paragraph order if you anchor on the wrong node or iterate over fragment children naively. Safer patterns are: (1) insert after the last paragraph of the target block, not the heading; (2) use a temporary marker/comment anchor; and (3) immediately verify the edited region with `read_file` around the insertion point before making more edits. - **Chapter reordering after expansion**: When chronology changes late in the process, reorder whole `
` blocks rather than trying to renumber content in place. {"success": true, "name": "memoir-publishing-workflow", "description": "Comprehensive approach for transforming raw memoirs into professionally formatted books with enhanced transitions, proper publishing details, and AI integration.", "tags": ["memoir", "publishing", "formatting", "transitions", "PDF", "HTML", "WeasyPrint", "OpenRouter", "AI-generation", "image-creation"], "related_skills": [], "content": "--- name: memoir-publishing-workflow version: 2.1.0 description: Comprehensive approach for transforming raw memoirs into professionally formatted books with enhanced transitions, proper publishing details, and AI integration. tags: [memoir, publishing, formatting, transitions, PDF, HTML, WeasyPrint, OpenRouter, AI-generation, image-creation] depends: [add_transitions_to_unwritten_future, manuscript-conversion-pipeline, manuscript-restructuring] --- # Memoir & Book Saga Publishing Pipeline ## Overview A high-production pipeline for multi-volume book series and memoirs, integrating cinematic AI-generated cover art, systematic front/back matter assembly, and professional PDF generation using ReportLab as a robust alternative to Pandoc. ## When to Use - Building professional-quality books or series for digital delivery. - When Pandoc or complex LaTeX environments are unavailable and a Python-native solution is needed. - Requiring consistent visual branding across a series (covers, typography). ## Workflow Steps ### 1. Visual Branding (Covers) - **Tooling:** Use `requests` with endpoints like `pollinations.ai` for reliable, no-key fallback image generation. - **Prompts:** Use cinematic descriptors ("hyper-realistic", "high contrast", "light band for title space") to ensure professional quality. - **Aspect Ratio:** Standard 2:3 portrait (1024x1536) for book covers. ### 2. Front & Back Matter - **Title Page:** Enshrine title, subtitle, author, and specific taglines. - **Copyright:** Include Standard placeholders: Year, Publisher, Rights Reserved note. - **Author Note:** Include a specific "Note on composition" or "AI Disclaimer" if assisted by agents. - **Back Cover:** Include praise placeholders, author bio, and standard identifiers (ISBN/Logo placeholders). ### 3. Professional PDF Generation (ReportLab) Since `pandoc` often fails due to complex dependencies or missing PDF engines, use a direct `ReportLab` implementation for total layout control: - **Margins:** 2.5cm standard for A4. - **Typography:** Use `Times-Roman` (12pt Body) and `Times-Bold` (18pt Headings) for the "bestseller" look. - **Justification:** Set `alignment=4` in `ParagraphStyle` for professional blocks. - **Dynamic TOC:** - Scan the manuscript for `## Chapter` headers. - Build a list of `Paragraph` items in the `story`. - **Media Delivery:** Always provide an absolute path for the final PDF to ensure `MEDIA:/path` works on Telegram. ## Example ReportLab Implementation ```python from reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak, Image from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4 from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet, ParagraphStyle from reportlab.lib.units import cm def build_book(md_path, cover_path, output_pdf): doc = SimpleDocTemplate(output_pdf, pagesize=A4, margins=2.5*cm) styles = getSampleStyleSheet() story = [Image(cover_path, width=16*cm, height=24*cm), PageBreak()] # ... logic to parse markdown and append PageBreaks at ## Chapter doc.build(story) ``` **Skill for:** Systematically transforming a raw memoir manuscript into a professionally formatted, published-quality book (HTML/PDF) with enhanced transitions, proper front/back matter, AI-generated images, and print-ready output. ## Overview This skill provides a comprehensive approach for converting raw memoir content into a print-ready format, including: - **Manuscript preparation** - Content review, editing, and structural organization - **Formatting & layout** - HTML/CSS styling for professional appearance - **Image generation** - AI-created chapter illustrations and cover art - **PDF conversion** - Multiple methods for print-ready output - **Quality assurance** - Verification and testing procedures - **Final publication polish** - Late-stage cleanup, exact pagination checks, and narrative consistency verification - **Delivery** - File preparation and distribution The workflow combines traditional publishing techniques with modern AI tools to create high-quality books efficiently. ## When to Use - When preparing a memoir for publication - When enhancing narrative flow with historical context - When formatting books for print or digital distribution - When working with limited formatting tools - When creating professional-quality books without expensive software ## Prerequisites - Raw manuscript content (Markdown or text format) - Basic understanding of book structure (front matter, chapters, back matter) - Access to image generation tools (OpenRouter recommended) - PDF conversion capability (WeasyPrint preferred, alternatives available) - Python environment for automation (optional but helpful) ## Phase 1: Manuscript Preparation ### Content Review Process 1. **Read through complete manuscript** to understand narrative flow and identify gaps 2. **Check for consistency** in voice, tense, and perspective throughout 3. **Verify historical facts** and timeline accuracy 4. **Evaluate transition quality** between chapters and parts 5. **Assess emotional impact** and reader engagement ### Editing Approach - **Structural editing**: Ensure logical chapter progression and proper sequencing - **Line editing**: Improve sentence flow, readability, and style - **Transition enhancement**: Replace placeholders with rich, personal reflections - **Fact-checking**: Verify historical events and personal details - **Sensitivity review**: Ensure respectful representation of all people and events - **Deduplication-first memoir merging**: When new story fragments arrive after a manuscript already exists, first audit the current manuscript to determine what is already present, what is only partially represented, and what is truly new. Merge only unique facts or sharper details; do not duplicate full stories already in the book. - **Insertion by narrative anchor**: In long HTML memoirs, avoid naive before/after-heading insertion when using BeautifulSoup or similar parsers. Anchoring directly on heading tags can accidentally reorder content. Instead, insert new subsections after the final paragraph of the intended logical block, then verify local ordering with spot reads. - **BeautifulSoup ordering pitfall**: In very large HTML files, repeated `insert_before` / `insert_after` operations with parsed fragments can still produce unexpected heading/paragraph order if you anchor on the wrong node or iterate over fragment children naively. Safer patterns are: (1) insert after the last paragraph of the target block, not the heading; (2) use a temporary marker/comment anchor; and (3) immediately verify the edited region with `read_file` around the insertion point before making more edits. - **Chapter reordering after expansion**: When chronology changes late in the process, reorder whole `
` blocks rather than trying to renumber content in place. After moving sections, regenerate the Table of Contents directly from the actual chapter order in the HTML so the TOC cannot drift from the manuscript structure. - **TOC pagination stabilization for print HTML/PDF**: In WeasyPrint-style book pipelines, a multi-page TOC can change later page numbers every time it is edited, because the TOC itself shifts the front matter length. The reliable workflow is: (1) clean up TOC layout first (dot leaders, indentation, continuation pages), (2) generate a PDF and extract actual chapter/subsection start pages, (3) write those numbers back into the TOC, and (4) avoid further TOC layout edits unless you are prepared to recompute all page numbers again. If exact publication page numbers matter, freeze TOC styling before the final mapping pass. - **TOC extraction false-positive pitfall**: When page numbers are extracted from PDF text, searching for a chapter title from page 1 can incorrectly match the TOC page instead of the real chapter page. A more reliable method is to insert hidden locator strings such as `CHAPTER_START_01` / `PART_START_01` into the body HTML, detect the first actual body page in the PDF, and only search for markers from that page forward. This prevents chapter-page mappings from collapsing onto TOC pages during automated rebuilds. - **Late-pass image replacement workflow**: For targeted chapter-image swaps in large final HTML files, replace only the relevant `` `src` attributes by chapter title, rebuild the PDF, then verify page count and title metadata. This is safer than regenerating the entire manuscript from earlier passes. - **Transition expansion workflow**: When asked to make transitions longer, treat them as miniature narrative essays rather than filler. Each should (a) begin from the emotional residue of the prior chapter, (b) explain what was happening historically in the wider world at that time, (c) connect that history back to Bob's lived experience in plain human language, and (d) point naturally toward the next chapter. In practice, ~2.5K–3K characters per transition can work well for a rich but readable bridge in HTML memoir format. - **Image-generation environment reality check**: Do not assume image API access is available just because Hermes config references OpenRouter or a vision model. Check the live environment first. If external image generation is unavailable, update the chapter prompt files anyway and either (a) produce temporary local sketch placeholders, clearly labeled as such, or (b) finish the manuscript/PDF and defer true regeneration to a follow-up pass. - **Telegram delivery fallback**: If direct `send_message(target='telegram')` fails because no Telegram home channel is configured, deliver book files in the assistant response using `MEDIA:/absolute/path` instead of stopping the workflow. - **Late-stage cleanup audit**: Before finalizing an expanded memoir, run a targeted audit for repeated story beats, duplicated exposition, chronology drift, and empty or near-empty subsection headings. Large embedded-image HTML files are too heavy to inspect casually; sample by chapter/region and, when useful, delegate a focused audit that returns exact subsection names to cut, merge, or move. - **Transition expansion standard**: For this style of memoir, transitions should often be several dense paragraphs rather than brief connectors. Humanize them by tying private emotional movement to the larger historical atmosphere of the period (Cold War anxiety, postwar prosperity, technology acceleration, etc.), but do not let them invent personal facts. - **Graceful degradation when image regeneration is blocked**: If the manuscript needs updated chapter sketches but image-generation credentials are unavailable in the active execution environment, still complete the editorial and print-ready pass. Refresh all image prompt files, preserve existing images, note the limitation clearly, and defer only the actual regeneration step. ### Key Deliverables - Clean, edited manuscript file (Markdown format) - Chapter-by-chapter analysis report - Transition quality assessment - Historical context verification - Sensitivity review notes ## Phase 2: Formatting & Layout ### HTML Structure ```html Memoir Title
...
...
...
...
...
...
...
...
...
...
...
``` ### CSS Styling Specifications ```css /* Base styles */ body { font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; margin: 2.5cm; /* Standard print margins */ line-height: 1.5; color: #333; max-width: 100%; hyphens: auto; } /* Page setup for A4 */ @page { size: A4; margin: 2.5cm; } /* Chapter headings */ .chapter { page-break-before: always; margin-top: 3cm; } .chapter-number { font-size: 2em; font-weight: bold; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.1em; margin-bottom: 0.5em; } .chapter-title { font-size: 1.5em; font-weight: normal; margin-bottom: 1em; } /* Transitions */ .transition { font-style: italic; margin: 2em 0; padding: 1em 2em; border-left: 3px solid #ccc; background: #f9f9f9; } /* Page numbers */ @bottom-center { content: counter(page); font-size: 0.9em; color: #666; } /* Headers */ @top-left { content: "The Future is Unwritten"; font-size: 0.8em; color: #999; } @top-right { content: "Robert Mills"; font-size: 0.8em; color: #999; } ``` ### Special Elements - **Transitions**: 10-20 sentence passages between chapters - **Historical context**: Integrated seamlessly into narrative - **Physiological effects**: Described in accessible, engaging language - **Images**: Placeholder positions with captions - **Drop caps**: First letter of each chapter enlarged and styled - **Part openings**: Special formatting for major section divisions ## Phase 3: Image Generation ### Image Types Required 1. **Cover Image** - Professional, eye-catching design 2. **Chapter Illustrations** - One per chapter (black and white sketches) 3. **Epilogue Image** - Reflective closing image ### Prompt Engineering Approach For each image, create specific prompts based on chapter content: **Cover Prompt Structure:** ``` Create a professional book cover for the memoir "[TITLE]" by [AUTHOR]. The cover should feature: - [Key visual elements representing main themes] - [Color scheme and mood description] - [Typography requirements] - [Style guidelines: modern/classic, minimal/detailed] - Aspect ratio: 2:3 (standard book cover) ``` **Chapter Sketch Prompt Structure:** ``` [Description of scene or symbol from chapter]. Style: Black and white pencil sketch, hand-drawn, with shading and texture, suitable for a memoir chapter header. ``` ### Image Integration - Save generated images as PNG files (300 DPI for print) - Place images at chapter beginnings (approx. 3-4 inches wide) - Add descriptive captions when appropriate - Ensure consistent style across all illustrations - Optimize file sizes for web and print versions ## Phase 4: PDF Conversion ### WeasyPrint Conversion ```python from weasyprint import HTML # Basic conversion HTML('manuscript.html').write_pdf('memoir.pdf') # With custom CSS for print-specific styling HTML('manuscript.html', stylesheets=['print.css']).write_pdf('memoir.pdf') # With additional options HTML( 'manuscript.html', stylesheets=['style.css', 'print.css'], url_fetcher=my_url_fetcher # For handling local image paths ).write_pdf( 'memoir.pdf', zoom=1.0, # Adjust as needed image_resolution=300 # DPI for images ) ``` ### Alternative Methods 1. **Browser Print**: Open HTML in browser and use "Print to PDF" 2. **wkhtmltopdf**: Command-line tool for batch processing ```bash wkhtmltopdf book.html book.pdf ``` 3. **Pandoc**: Universal document converter ```bash pandoc book.html -o book.pdf ``` 4. **PrinceXML**: Commercial alternative with excellent CSS support ```bash prince book.html -o book.pdf ``` ### Print-Ready Settings - **Bleeds**: 0.125 inches (if required by printer) - **Resolution**: 300 DPI for images - **Color Profile**: CMYK for professional printing - **Fonts**: Embed all fonts or use web-safe alternatives - **Accessibility**: Add semantic HTML structure for screen readers ## Phase 5: Quality Assurance ### Content Verification Checklist - [ ] All chapters present and in correct order - [ ] Transitions are meaningful and well-placed - [ ] Images match chapter content and are properly positioned - [ ] Page numbers correct and consistent throughout - [ ] Table of contents matches chapter pages - [ ] Front matter properly formatted and in correct order - [ ] Copyright and ISBN information included - [ ] Back matter complete (epilogue, author bio, etc.) - [ ] New material does not duplicate stories already present in the manuscript - [ ] New subsections appear in the intended chronological location after insertion - [ ] Rewritten additions preserve original facts and characters while improving prose style ### Technical Checks - [ ] PDF renders correctly on multiple devices and PDF readers - [ ] Fonts display properly (embedded/embeddable) - [ ] Images are high resolution (300 DPI) and clear - [ ] Margins are correct for chosen printer specifications - [ ] No text is cut off or obscured by images - [ ] Hyperlinks work correctly (if digital version) - [ ] File size appropriate for distribution method ### Proofreading - [ ] Spelling and grammar checked using multiple tools - [ ] Punctuation consistent throughout document - [ ] Capitalization follows style guide - [ ] Chapter titles match across all instances - [ ] Page breaks occur at appropriate locations - [ ] No widows/orphans in text blocks - [ ] Consistent use of italics/bold for emphasis ### Final Publication Polish Pass Do one explicit last pass after the main edit/build cycle and before delivery. **Purpose:** catch the subtle issues that survive normal proofreading — chronology drift after late insertions, duplicate story beats after memoir merging, empty subsection headings, dangling production notes, TOC/page-number drift, and small wording inconsistencies introduced during rebuilds. **Workflow:** 1. **Freeze structure first** — avoid adding new stories or changing TOC styling during this pass unless absolutely necessary. 2. **Audit for duplication and chronology drift** — confirm newly merged material adds unique information rather than repeating existing scenes. 3. **Run a style and grammar sweep** — fix lingering punctuation, capitalization, hyphenation, POV slips, and awkward repeated phrasing. 4. **Check print artifacts** — remove leftover placeholders, empty headings, editor notes, stray "end of manuscript" lines, and layout debris. 5. **Verify TOC stability** — if the TOC includes exact page numbers, calculate them from the near-final PDF after TOC styling is already frozen. If the TOC changes length again, recalculate. 6. **Spot-check chapter openings and image placement** — ensure each chapter starts cleanly, the correct sketch is attached, and no image has migrated into front matter or the TOC. 7. **Rebuild once more** — generate the final HTML/PDF pair and do a last spot-check of front matter, TOC pages, chapter numbering, and back matter. **Required outputs of the polish pass:** - Clean final HTML source - Final print-ready PDF - Rebuilt TOC reflecting the actual chapter order - Short note of any unresolved pagination caveats if TOC numbers cannot be frozen exactly in the current pipeline **Common fixes in this pass:** - Converting accidental first-person slips back to Bob-centric narration - Harmonizing names, dates, bases, institutions, and family references - Removing duplicate headings/subsections created during merges - Fixing nested TOC indentation and dot leaders - Removing leftover production text or scaffolding - Correcting chapter-image mismatches after late image swaps ## Phase 6: Delivery ### File Preparation - **Print PDF**: High-resolution, CMYK color profile, proper bleeds - **Ebook PDF**: Optimized for screen reading, smaller file size - **Source Files**: HTML, CSS, and Markdown originals - **Image Files**: Original AI-generated images and optimized versions - Use historical events to provide context, not overwhelm - Balance personal stories with broader themes - Show, don't tell - use sensory details and specific examples - Maintain consistent voice throughout the memoir ### Technical Implementation - Test PDF conversion early and often with sample chapters - Keep original AI prompts for future image regeneration - Maintain version control for all manuscript iterations - Create backup copies of all generated files -
